original_test_intent: Verify `TEMP_MB_OUTLET` is the correct motherboard outlet-air sensing point and is human-readable in Dashboard and Server Health > Sensor Reading with the expected value, units, health state and supported thresholds from the platform specification.
original_method: Resolve the stable outlet sensor and its physical placement, collect its complete read-only record and unchanged UI representations, and compare them with a co-located approved reference and specification under recorded chassis load, fan and airflow conditions. Preserve all logs and settings.
manual_activity: The platform owner identifies the physical motherboard outlet sensing point and defines the co-located reference, tolerances and operating conditions. Automation can collect the stable record and both UI views; a human verifies probe placement/airflow interpretation and owns the verdict. No fan, load or environmental change is authorized.
required_inputs: Exact chassis/board/BMC/BIOS configuration and motherboard outlet-sensor placement within the airflow path
Stable SDR name/number/type/entity/instance and corresponding Dashboard and Server Health rows
Expected Celsius scaling/rounding, allowed range or delta, threshold capability/values/hysteresis, health and unavailable semantics
Calibrated reference device, calibration validity, probe placement, sampling window, combined uncertainty and allowed BMC update lag
Recorded fan policy/speeds, system load/power state, inlet condition, panel/duct configuration and timestamp alignment
Validated ipmitool/API/browser versions, supported transport/cipher and protected authentication
Pinned immutable accessible `sensor.git` revision/checksum with safety review, or approved manual collection method
safety_requirements: Do not clear SEL or system logs; existing fan, thermal and platform events are relevant comparison context and clearing is unrelated to this passive check.
Do not infer physical outlet placement from the label. Confirm the board diagram and sensing point, and do not substitute chassis exhaust, PSU exhaust, inlet ambient or CPU package telemetry.
Use a co-located reference and approved uncertainty/lag model; room ambient alone is not an equivalent outlet reference because heat pickup depends on board load and airflow.
Do not change fan policy, block/open airflow, add workload, heat the system or modify thresholds. Record the natural operating state; dynamic response belongs to a separate approved test.

Respect the SDR threshold capability mask and preserve status, units, scaling and timestamp. A readable value is not sufficient if it is stale, mapped to the wrong location or missing required limits.

Do not truncate fallback inventory, expose passwords through `-P`, assume cipher 17 or execute the unavailable internal Script before review. Stop without automatic retry on duplicate identity, stale data or UI/OOB/reference disagreement.
agent_execution_scope: Validate target identity, outlet placement, client, reference and Script; establish the expected sensor/UI/spec mapping before collection.
Capture the complete raw/API record and unchanged Dashboard plus Server Health rows with identity, value, units, supported thresholds, status and timestamps.
Synchronize a co-located reference sample and record load/fan/airflow state, then calculate the approved difference including sensor/reference uncertainty and update lag.
Preserve redacted evidence and logs; make no clear, fan/load/environment/threshold change, automatic retry or DUT verdict.
engineer_actions: Approve the exact motherboard outlet sensing point and distinguish it from inlet, chassis and PSU exhaust locations.
Provide the value/threshold/status/freshness specification, reference probe placement and combined tolerance under named operating conditions, and approve the Script/tool.
Assess raw, UI and reference evidence and issue the formal verdict, recognizing that this passive point does not cover dynamic thermal control.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The literal sensor query can retrieve a record if the name is exact, but it cannot establish physical placement, operating/reference conditions or UI/spec agreement. `head -100` is not complete evidence, and the command exposes credentials and assumes cipher support.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Resolve the stable TEMP_MB_OUTLET record through complete inventory, retrieve it with protected read-only access, capture both UI locations and compare a time-aligned co-located reference under the approved fan/load/airflow state.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: TEMP_MB_OUTLET, Dashboard and Server Health > Sensor Reading, readability/specification Criteria, generic clear text, Script URL, DeepSeek commands and 1/0-minute estimates remain preserved; the Review layer adds location/reference controls without editing Master or changing the environment.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Correlate a stable outlet SDR identity and both UI rows with a time-aligned calibrated probe located at the specified board outlet, documenting load, fan and airflow state and comparing value/status/thresholds using a versioned tolerance model.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: The exact chassis/board/cooling configuration and BMC/SDR/WebUI build documented by the Project.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record chassis/board, BIOS/BMC/SDR/WebUI, fan policy, management client, reference-instrument calibration and Script revisions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Board sensor-placement and airflow drawings, outlet-sensor SDR/thermal specification, WebUI schema, instrument calibration and Project configuration specification.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds proof of outlet identity, co-located reference and operating context while preserving the passive sensor/UI comparison and source method.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: One passive outlet reading does not validate full chassis exhaust distribution, response across workload, threshold events, fan-control behavior or over-temperature protection.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Location/airflow map, sensor/spec thresholds, co-located reference/tolerance/timing rules, operating-state record, protected tool or reviewed Script and evidence contract.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Outlet gradients and recirculation can make room ambient misleading; UI rounding and BMC update delay can produce benign instantaneous differences.

project_override_considerations: A Project may use Redfish/OEM telemetry as an approved alternative to ipmitool only with the original method preserved, interface/version and reason recorded, engineer approval and equivalent outlet identity, value, threshold, status and freshness evidence. An inlet or chassis-exhaust sensor cannot replace the specified motherboard outlet point.
expected_evidence: Chassis/board/BMC/BIOS identity, cooling configuration and diagram/photo identifying the precise TEMP_MB_OUTLET sensing and reference points
Complete raw/API record with stable ID, value, units, threshold capabilities/values, status and timestamp
Redacted Dashboard and Server Health evidence with exact field mapping to that same sensor
Calibrated co-located reference samples, fan/load/power/airflow state, timestamps and combined tolerance/update-lag calculation
Project specification comparison, any stale/location/UI divergence disposition and pinned Script/tool security evidence
No-clear/no-write/no-airflow-or-load-change/no-retry proof, final health, limitations and engineer-owned verdict

review_improvement: Prevents a plausible but wrongly located or stale temperature from being accepted as motherboard outlet coverage and prevents an uncontrolled room-ambient comparison from producing a false verdict.
independent_technical_reasoning: Outlet temperature is position- and airflow-dependent. A correct-looking value may come from a nearby but different sensing point, and room ambient does not include system heat rise. Identity therefore requires a board location map, while accuracy comparison requires a co-located calibrated reference, synchronized timestamps and known fan/load state; passive evidence cannot establish dynamic thermal protection.
